subject.title: South Orange County Community College District Board, Trustee Area 4

text: Military Officer/Educator

I, John Black, serving years as a Lieutenant Colonel, U.S. Marine Corps, believe South Orange County's community colleges should open doors to good careers, four-year universities, skilled trades, military, public service, and entrepreneurship. I am running for the Board of Trustees to help students succeed while protecting taxpayer dollars.

I have spent my career as an educator, teaching, coaching, and mentoring students, including Marines, and serving as adjunct faculty, a distinguished fellow at MIT, and guest lecturer at universities. Learning changes lives; I have spent decades helping people learn, lead, and grow.

I have led large organizations and managed the public funds that support them. As Senior Emergency Management Program Coordinator for the Orange County Health Care Agency, I strengthened disaster preparedness, improved accountability for funded programs, and coordinated planning serving millions of residents. I understand budgets, oversight, and stewardship of public resources.
I co-lead The JASSD Group and support veterans, first responders, and their families through Veterans FORWARD. My wife, Dr. Aime Black, our family, and I live in San Clemente.
As a Trustee, I will focus on student success, academic excellence, workforce partnerships, safe campuses, and transparent governance.
I would be honored to serve and respectfully ask for your vote.
www.johnblack4collegeboard.com

text: Executive Dean
It is an honor to seek your vote for the South Orange County Community College District Board of Trustees.

For more than 30 years, I have dedicated my career to public higher education. I have had the privilege of serving as a dean at both Irvine Valley College and Saddleback College, working alongside faculty, staff, administrators, and community partners to expand educational opportunities and strengthen our colleges.

As Executive Dean of Extended Learning at Saddleback College, I oversee programs that provide lifelong learning, workforce training, adult education, and community education to thousands of students each year. I have managed multimillion-dollar budgets, secured grant funding, and developed partnerships that prepare students for meaningful careers while meeting local workforce needs.

As your trustee, I will promote academic excellence, student success, fiscal responsibility, and accountability. I believe public service means listening, making thoughtful decisions, respecting diverse perspectives, and ensuring responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars. My commitment is to preserve the district’s tradition of excellence while expanding opportunities that benefit students, employees, employers, and our community.
I bring experience, integrity, and a collaborative approach to governance. I would be honored to earn your trust and your vote.

text: Board Member, Capistrano Unified School District
Tested Leadership – Future Focus – Transparency

During my twelve-year tenure on your Capistrano Unified School District board, I successfully advocated for the establishment of a new Academy for CUSD students, located on the Saddleback College campus, where students are able to take both high school and college courses, and may simultaneously earn CUSD and Saddleback diplomas.

I was part of the team that hired a new superintendent; added to the already-strong Honors, Advanced Placement, and International Baccalaureate curricula; improved public transparency and communication with parents; and many other accomplishments.

It’s critical that we prepare students for a very rapidly changing global economy and job market. I’ll urgently advocate for coursework in emerging fields, as well as high-demand careers with apprenticeship options, both for young people and those pursuing new fields of work or study.

Public trust requires stringent oversight. The current South Orange County Community College District board failed to protect residents and taxpayers when they voted to accept a $750,000 developer inducement tied to a potentially hazardous Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), near Saddleback College, without proper scrutiny. Trustees must independently vet staff recommendations rather than rubber-stamping staff proposals that may compromise community safety.
If elected, I’ll bring governance experience, future-driven vision, and public accountability to the board. 949-371-6662

text: College Dean/Educator

I'm Narges Rakin — an educator, a professor, a parent, and an advocate who has spent nearly three decades working inside California's community colleges, putting students first as a tenured professor, a faculty union negotiator, and now a Dean. That depth of experience is an asset, not just a resume line because I know this system inside and out, from the classroom to the negotiating table to the administration building, and I know where the gaps between promises and practice tend to show up.

I'm running for the SOCCCD Board of Trustees because I believe our district's budget and decisions belong to the public, not just the boardroom. Too often, families are asked to trust institutions without being shown the reasoning behind them. I don't think that's good enough.

As a board member, I will push for open, plain-language budget reporting that any parent or taxpayer can actually read. I will prioritize outside grant and workforce-development funding to grow academic programs, protecting the general fund as a last resort. And I will insist that every decision can stand up to a direct question from a student, a parent, or the public — asked openly, and answered honestly.
I ask for your vote.
www.therakin.org
